task.description: Idiom-review the diff on feature/WF02-REQ033-20260817 (git diff main...HEAD, lib/letflow/definitions/snapshot_store.ex). SECURITY-REVIEWER already PASSed INV-1..INV-8. result.summary:
Read the full diff (git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/definitions/snapshot_store.ex, 216-line new file), the full design doc (lib/letflow/design/req033-snapshot-store.md), REQ-033's exact requirement-yaml entry (docs/requirements.yaml:1514-1554, not the design doc's paraphrase), InstanceDefinitionSnapshot's schema module, ProcessDefinition's tenant_id column, event_store.ex's fetch_uuid/3 and instance_sequence locking code for comparison, and docs/anti-patterns.md (3 entries, none apply to this diff). Ran `mix compile --force` on this host: clean, 48 files, no warnings -- a real toolchain confirmation, not a can't-verify fallback.

OQ-2 (idempotency: does a retry with a DIFFERENT definition_id need a distinct {:error, :definition_id_mismatch}?) -- CONFIRMED ACCEPTABLE AS BUILT, not the same failure class as REQ-025's tenant_id precedent, non-blocking. Reasoning: (1) REQ-033's own requirement text (docs/requirements.yaml:1524-1526) names the exact SQL mechanism, not just an intent: 'ON CONFLICT (instance_id) DO NOTHING semantics for idempotency (a retry of the same instance_id's snapshot creation is a no-op, not a second row)'. ON CONFLICT (instance_id) DO NOTHING is, by construction, a single-column arbiter -- it does not evaluate the other columns of the conflicting row at all, so there is no natural point in that SQL statement to compare definition_id without adding an extra read the requirement's own text does not describe. Implementing literally what the requirement names is not a crutch; it is the correct reading. (2) AC2's literal wording ('called twice with the same instance_id is idempotent ... OR returns a distinct SnapshotAlreadyExists-equivalent error -- pick one, state which') is genuinely silent on the differing-definition_id sub-case -- it does not resolve OQ-2 either way, so this was correctly left as a real open question for this gate rather than something the design doc could have cited as settling it. (3) Distinguishing this from REQ-025's tenant_id case, which I independently re-examined (event_store.ex's reject_tenant_id/1, lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md, and my own REQ-025 Step 2d re-validation, handoffs/WF02-REQ025-20260817/step-02d-reviewer.json): that case was governed by a project-wide decision record (docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md's addendum) establishing a hard security invariant -- a caller-supplied tenant_id can misattribute a row to the wrong physical tenant schema, which is exactly the class of defect security-invariants.md's INV-1 exists to prevent, and the addendum settled it project-wide, not just for REQ-025. There is no equivalent decision record here, and no tenant-crossing risk: both definition_ids in a same-instance_id retry are necessarily read and written within the same opts[:prefix] schema (SnapshotStore never accepts or derives a schema per definition_id), so a mismatch, however it arose, cannot cross a tenant boundary -- it is purely an application-level 'which of two possibly-legitimate values wins' question, not a security defect. (4) The moduledoc documents this choice transparently (not silently): the 'Deliberate divergence' section states the on_conflict: :nothing behavior plainly, and OQ-2 is restated for REVIEWER rather than quietly assumed resolved. Given (1)-(4), requiring a definition_id-comparison read here would be adding behavior the requirement's own text does not ask for, ahead of any concrete caller that would need it (S3's EE-01 engine doesn't exist yet) -- which is itself the kind of premature-elaboration this gate's own scope-creep question exists to catch, just pointed the other direction from usual. NON-BLOCKING RECOMMENDATION (route as a note, not rework): TEST-DESIGNER should add an explicit test pinning this exact behavior (create/3 called twice for the same instance_id with two different definition_ids returns {:ok, <the FIRST snapshot, unchanged>}, not an error, and inserts zero additional rows) so the deliberate silent-discard semantics are demonstrated in the test suite, not only asserted in prose -- and S3's own EE-01 engine design (when it exists) should independently decide whether the ENGINE layer, which actually knows the intended definition_id semantically, needs a defensive comparison before or after calling create/3, since SnapshotStore itself has no way to know which of two definition_ids a caller 'meant'.

OQ-3 (FOR SHARE vs FOR UPDATE) -- CONFIRMED: FOR SHARE is the idiomatically correct lock mode here. Postgres FOR SHARE takes a non-exclusive row lock: it blocks a concurrent UPDATE/DELETE/FOR UPDATE against the same row while permitting other concurrent FOR SHARE holders to coexist. FOR UPDATE takes an exclusive lock and is reserved (in this codebase's own established idiom -- see event_store.ex's instance_sequence FOR UPDATE, lib/letflow/event_store/instance_sequence.ex's moduledoc, and req023/req025's design docs) for a row the current transaction intends to modify itself. locked_source_definition/2 never writes process_definitions -- it only reads name/version/graph to copy into the snapshot -- so FOR UPDATE would be strictly wrong here: it would serialize every concurrent create/3 call against the same definition_id even though none of them write that row, manufacturing artificial contention (e.g. many instances starting from the same popular process definition at once would needlessly queue on each other's locks). FOR SHARE lets all of those proceed concurrently while still blocking the one thing that actually matters -- a concurrent DELETE (AC4) or a hypothetical concurrent exclusive-lock write racing the snapshot's read -- from completing mid-capture. This matches REQ-033's own requirement text verbatim ('prevents a concurrent delete or exclusive-lock write from racing the snapshot capture') and is internally consistent with how this same codebase already draws the FOR SHARE/FOR UPDATE line elsewhere (event_store.ex's instance_sequence row, which IS written, correctly uses FOR UPDATE). Composed via Ecto.Query.lock/2 (`lock("FOR SHARE")`), not a raw SQL string -- INV-7-consistent, already independently confirmed by SECURITY-REVIEWER's to_sql probe.

INV-8 Ecto.UUID.cast/1 guard (cast_uuid/2, snapshot_store.ex lines ~150-159) -- idiom/consistency check: NOT a one-off patch, it is the established codebase idiom applied identically. Compared byte-for-byte against event_store.ex's fetch_uuid/3 (lines 191-202): both do `case Ecto.UUID.cast(value) do {:ok, uuid} -> {:ok, uuid}; :error -> {:error, error_reason} end`, the only difference being fetch_uuid/3 first pulls the value out of an attrs map (event_store.ex's calling convention takes a map) while cast_uuid/2 takes the value directly (snapshot_store.ex's calling convention is positional args) -- a difference in calling convention, not in the guard mechanism itself. Applied consistently at every entry point that accepts a caller-supplied UUID-shaped value in this module: both instance_id and definition_id in create/3, and instance_id in get_by_instance_id/2. This is the third module in this codebase now using Ecto.UUID.cast/1 as the standard external-I/O boundary guard for UUID-shaped input (after event_store.ex's fetch_uuid/3) -- worth naming explicitly as a codebase idiom now, not just a recurring coincidence, though not yet worth extracting into a shared helper (two call sites with slightly different calling conventions is not yet a strong enough signal to justify that abstraction -- watch for a third differently-shaped call site before extracting).

Idiomatic vs. crutch (general): the module is a plain context module using Repo.transaction/2 with an anonymous function (not Ecto.Multi) for a two-step, single-lock-lifetime transaction -- the design doc's own §6.2 argues explicitly for why Multi's step-naming machinery is unneeded for exactly two dependent steps, and I agree: introducing Multi here for two steps sharing one lock would be machinery ahead of need, the inverse mistake to what OQ-2's discussion above cautions against. The insert-then-reselect-by-primary-key pattern (L2/L3) is a simplified, correctly-scoped reuse of the idiom req025-event-append.md established for the identical on_conflict: :nothing ambiguity -- appropriately simpler here since instance_id is the table's own primary key (no surrogate id needed). No hand-rolled retry loops, no racy check-then-write pattern, no raw SQL. This is real idiomatic Ecto/OTP usage, not a GenServer-shaped crutch standing in for something else.

Supervision -- N/A, confirmed explicitly, not assumed. Grepped the diff for GenServer/Supervisor/gen_statem/spawn/Registry/InstanceSupervisor: zero hits. SnapshotStore is a stateless context module with no process, no registration, and no interaction with Letflow.InstanceSupervisor -- correctly so, since this module has no per-instance runtime state to isolate; it is a pure DB-access layer over two already-supervised-by-Postgres tables.

Type-safety gaps (noted per the standing instruction, not blocking): (a) OQ-2's core gap IS a type-safety gap in the sense the task asks about -- a stricter type system could express 'definition_id is a write-once field, and this function's contract guarantees the argument matches the stored value or fails' as a refinement/dependent type on the return value, catching a caller's stale-argument bug at the call site instead of silently returning divergent data with no signal; Elixir's type system (even with the incoming set-theoretic types) has no natural way to encode 'this success value's field equals one of my two inputs, and I am not telling you which, nor whether they agreed' -- this is exactly the class of gap the task explicitly asks to have named even when the design was otherwise correct. (b) create_error()'s Ecto.Changeset.t() | term() catch-all (§4.3, unchanged from the design) is the same un-exhaustive-checked catch-all shape flagged in my REQ-025 review -- still just a watch item, same reasoning applies here: a future 7th failure mode would silently route through the generic clause rather than forcing a compile-time exhaustiveness check.

Scope creep -- none found. No new behaviours, macros, or generic plumbing. The module builds exactly create/3 and get_by_instance_id/2, matching the design doc's §1 scope boundary table, and explicitly declines to build the EE-01 engine integration point, process_definitions CRUD, or graph validation -- all correctly deferred to their owning requirements/stages per the moduledoc's own S3-scope-boundary section. Choosing NOT to add a definition_id-mismatch check (OQ-2, above) is, if anything, evidence against scope creep, not for it.

docs/anti-patterns.md -- re-checked in full (3 entries: Docker toolchain workaround, requirement_status.yaml overwrite, handoff timestamp estimation). None apply to this diff.

Overall verdict: PASS. Both open questions explicitly resolved with reasoning (OQ-2 accepted as-built, distinguished from the REQ-025 tenant_id precedent on the merits rather than by surface-shape analogy; OQ-3 confirmed FOR SHARE is correct). INV-8 guard confirmed as consistent codebase idiom, not a crutch. One non-blocking recommendation for TEST-DESIGNER (pin the OQ-2 retry-with-different-definition_id behavior explicitly in a test) carried forward as a note, not a blocking issue.

issues.summary: create/3's idempotency check keys purely on instance_id (ON CONFLICT (instance_id) DO NOTHING); a retry supplying a different definition_id than the already-stored snapshot silently returns the original snapshot, no error, no signal of disagreement.
issues.recommendation: CONFIRMED ACCEPTABLE AS BUILT -- matches REQ-033's own requirement text naming this exact SQL mechanism, and is not governed by any decision record the way REQ-025's tenant_id attribution case was (no tenant-crossing risk, no INV-1-class defect). Non-blocking follow-up: TEST-DESIGNER should add an explicit test pinning this behavior (retry with a different definition_id returns the original snapshot unchanged, zero additional rows). S3's future EE-01 engine design should independently decide whether the engine layer needs its own defensive check before calling create/3 a second time with a different definition_id.

issues.summary: L1's locked read of process_definitions uses FOR SHARE, not FOR UPDATE, chosen from requirement text alone (R-Co source unreachable).
issues.recommendation: CONFIRMED CORRECT -- FOR SHARE is the right choice for a read-only guard against concurrent delete/exclusive-lock write on a row this module never itself modifies; FOR UPDATE would be wrong (unnecessary write-intent lock, would serialize unrelated concurrent create/3 calls against the same definition_id). Consistent with this codebase's existing FOR UPDATE usage for a row it does write (event_store.ex's instance_sequence).

issues.summary: The write-once/first-writer-wins guarantee for definition_id is enforced only by SQL semantics (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) plus code review, not by any type-level contract -- a stricter type system could in principle surface a caller's stale-argument bug at the call site; Elixir cannot express this.
issues.recommendation: No action required now; same class of accepted tradeoff as the REQ-025 Multi-step-ordering watch item. Revisit only if S3's EE-01 engine design finds this gap causes a real incident.
